analysis:
The PR changes only CI test scripts (scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py and scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py). It touches no provider, coordinator, crypto, attestation or cache code, so the provider/native-runtime threat model (A-001..A-020, TB-002..TB-014, T-041) is not affected directly. The changes drop the `required` flag from the build-cluster, build-provider and cluster-release-checks lanes (PLAN_LANES, lines 107-109). Build lanes now ask the plane without a size while job sizes are off, instead of staying on Blacksmith. The test expectations and comments are updated to match. The assertions in provider-ci-workflow (lines ~727-730, ~825-828) now expect lane lines without ` required`. The corresponding workflow YAML (provider-plan.yml, provider-tests.yml) is not in the supplied batch, so the new routing behavior itself is unverified here.

Security-relevant checks that remain in the test suite and that I reviewed: the router uses TLS verification and https-only URLs. It sends nothing for fork PRs. It accepts only exact label arrays. It prevents injection of plane text into workflow commands and markdown. Routed jobs keep read-only permissions and bounded timeouts. Release and credentialed workflows keep literal runners with no self-hosted labels. The tests do not weaken these controls. Dropping `required` means build lanes, which may feed release-adjacent caches, could run on self-hosted Darkbloom runners when sizes are off. Those jobs are asserted read-only, and the release workflows stay unrouted (UNROUTED list, lines 142-144, and the test at line 940). No concrete regression is evident. The remaining question for integration is whether the unseen workflow YAML matches these expectations. That is a CI-consistency issue, not something demonstrated here to be a vulnerability.
